questions: Did this problem start after a recent head injury or accident?
Do you have double vision when looking straight ahead?
Is your right eye unable to move outward (towards the right)?
Does your right eyelid droop significantly?
Is your right pupil larger than your left pupil?
Do you have severe pain around your right eye or forehead?
Have you been diagnosed with diabetes or high blood pressure?
Did this condition come on suddenly, over hours or days?

results: 1. Measure the vertical deviation in primary gaze and assess for limitation of upgaze in the affected eye
2. Perform a forced duction test on the right eye to check for mechanical restriction
forced duction test: restriction consistent with a mechanical cause
3. Obtain a non-contrast CT scan of the head and orbits with bone windows
CT head (non-contrast): multiple skull fractures and epidural haemorrhage; NO evidence of brainstem injury
4. Obtain an MRI of the brain and orbits
MRI sella and orbits: subtle MEDIAL ORBITAL WALL FRACTURE with medial rectus involvement; no brainstem pathology
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic entrapment of the medial rectus muscle secondary to a medial orbital wall fracture
Alternative 1: Orbital floor fracture with inferior rectus entrapment (blowout fracture)
Alternative 2: Post-traumatic restrictive strabismus due to soft tissue scarring
